# FieldWrapper

The label, description, helper text, and error message that surround a form control — without the control itself.

- **Import:** `import { FieldWrapper, FormField } from "@kozmos-ds/react";`
- **Group:** Components
- **Platforms:** React, SwiftUI and Compose; linked to its Figma component through Code Connect.
- **Storybook:** <https://vodoco.github.io/kozmos-design-system/storybook/?path=/docs/components-fieldwrapper--docs>

## Example

From its `Default` story.

```tsx
import { FieldWrapper, Input, ThemeProvider } from "@kozmos-ds/react";

export function FieldWrapperExample() {
  return (
    <ThemeProvider defaultTheme="light">
      <FieldWrapper
        description="Use supporting guidance when the field needs it."
        helperText="Helper text"
        label="Label"
        required
        status="default"
        className="w-80"
      >
        <Input placeholder="Placeholder" />
      </FieldWrapper>
    </ThemeProvider>
  );
}
```

## FieldWrapper

It forwards its ref to `HTMLDivElement`. Its props are `FieldWrapperProps`, which extends `React.HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>`.

- `description`: `React.ReactNode`, optional.
- `descriptionId`: `string`, optional.
- `error`: `boolean | string`, optional.
- `errorId`: `string`, optional.
- `helperText`: `string`, optional.
- `helperId`: `string`, optional.
- `hideLabel`: `boolean`, optional.
- `label`: `string`, optional.
- `labelAction`: `React.ReactNode`, optional.
- `inputId`: `string`, optional.
- `group`: `boolean`, optional, default `false`.

  Name a group of individually labelled controls, not one input.

- `optionalText`: `string`, optional.
- `required`: `boolean`, optional.
- `status`: `FieldStatus`, optional, default `"default"`.
- `count`: `React.ReactNode`, optional.

  A character count, drawn on the message line.

  It sits BEFORE the message and inside the same element, so the count and
  the reason read as one thing — "28/512 · Please enter at least 50
  characters." — rather than as two stray fragments.

  When there is no message the count is drawn in a plain paragraph with no
  role. It must not land in the `role="alert"` element: the count changes on
  every keystroke, and an assertive region would make a screen reader read
  the number back after each letter typed.

- `countId`: `string`, optional.
- `children`: `React.ReactNode`, **required**.

It also takes the attributes React's DOM types give it (`className`, `style`, `id`, `aria-*`, the event handlers among them).

## Types these props take

### FieldStatus

From `@kozmos-ds/react`.

```ts
type FieldStatus = "default" | "error" | "warning" | "success";
```
